nodes.label: There are no milestones any more
nodes.rationale: Thirteen numbered milestones were the right shape for a kernel that did not boot yet, and the numbers went on being quoted long after they described anything: the README said M6, graphics while the machine had a journalled filesystem, a TCP/IP stack and a web browser. A number that no longer means anything is worse than no number, because it is read as though it does.

nodes.label: The kernel, built
nodes.rationale: 39-bit virtual addresses through three levels of long-descriptor tables, exceptions and a vector table, a timer, the GIC, strict priority bands with immediate preemption, and lazy FP save - a thread that never touches a floating-point register never pays for one.

nodes.label: Lazy FP save
nodes.rationale: Every kernel thread never touches a floating-point register by construction, so it never pays for one.

nodes.label: A filesystem of its own, with a journal
nodes.rationale: Checked against power loss by killing the machine at an exact instant rather than hoping. Attributes on files, and live queries over them.

nodes.label: Graphics, built
nodes.rationale: Surfaces with C pixel loops, outline fonts rasterised on demand from TrueType, UTF-8 throughout, and a compositor. Windows are drawing commands by default and a shared double-buffered surface when an application asks.

nodes.label: A desktop, built
nodes.rationale: A window manager with menus, resizing, scrollbars and stacking; a widget kit; themes; the Deskbar; Tracker; a terminal; and replicants.

nodes.label: Networking, built
nodes.rationale: virtio-net, ARP, IP, ICMP and TCP with shared rings, an HTTP server, a telnet client. It reaches the real internet through QEMU's NAT.

nodes.label: Audio, built
nodes.rationale: virtio-snd, a mixer, WAV and MP3.

nodes.label: A web browser
nodes.rationale: hubbub, libdom and libcss running at EL0: HTML parsed into a DOM, the CSS cascade run with a user-agent stylesheet, text laid out into boxes that survive the paint, and links you can click.

nodes.label: Tooling: test, screenshot, bench, stress, release
A resolver
nodes.rationale: An address is four numbers today, which is the single biggest thing between the browser and the web. UDP exists in the stack only as much as DNS needs - no sockets, because nothing else has asked for any.

nodes.label: A non-blocking send
nodes.rationale: Half a browser frame is the application blocked on a commit whose handler swaps an index and records a rectangle. SYS_CALL, SYS_RECEIVE and SYS_REPLY are the whole IPC surface and every message blocks for its reply by construction, so triple buffering cannot fix it. It is a change to the IPC model: a syscall, a fixed-size queue in the endpoint struct, a decision about what a full queue does, and backpressure.

nodes.label: x86-64, under QEMU - done
nodes.rationale: All thirteen kernel/*.c compile for it with no #ifdef, and the whole userland - fifty thousand lines - needed about a hundred and ten lines of assembly and one #if. The 64-bit line was drawn where it was precisely so this would not be a refactor.

nodes.label: hal/virtio - shared drivers, per-board transport
nodes.rationale: The four virtio drivers moved into a shared directory rather than being rewritten, with each board bringing its own transport: fixed offsets from a device-tree window on one, a walk of the PCI capability list on the other. Same sequence, every register somewhere else.

nodes.label: The scan that reset the keyboard on its way past
nodes.rationale: The worst of the port's bugs was not about x86 at all: it was latent on ARM too, and survived only because QEMU happens to lay virtio-mmio windows out in the reverse of the order the devices are given.

nodes.label: SMP, and real parallelism
nodes.rationale: The x86-64 port paid part of it forward: two pieces of state are per-CPU rather than per-thread - the TSS and whoever owns the floating-point registers - and finding the boundary was not theoretical. A global holding the interrupted stack pointer looked like per-CPU state, was per-thread, and produced a process returning to user level on another process's stack.

nodes.label: PowerPC, on a G5 or a G4 iMac
nodes.rationale: It changes two things written down as settled: it is big-endian, and the G4 is 32-bit against a principle that says Kosmos is 64-bit only. The rule for a principle in the way is to say which one, say what it costs, and decide deliberately rather than drift.

nodes.label: The big-endian audit
nodes.rationale: Done before there was any reason to need it and it holds: every string.pack in the on-disk format carries an explicit <, a tree-wide search for native-endian packs finds none, and the network stack builds big-endian by construction with byte shifts. What would move is runtime/include/endian.h, which becomes per-architecture.

nodes.label: Real hardware, a Raspberry Pi 5
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it is hard: a desktop that feels fast on it is a result rather than an emulator number. Every performance question is currently answered 'measure it on the Pi', and the Pi is not here yet.

nodes.label: A box model
nodes.rationale: Margins, padding, borders, width, floats. Images and forms both wait on it.

nodes.label: Images in the browser
nodes.rationale: stb_image is already vendored for the PDF reader.

nodes.label: Forms
nodes.rationale: They need a box that takes keys.

nodes.label: TLS
nodes.rationale: Without it most of the web refuses to speak.

nodes.label: An ELF loader
nodes.rationale: So a program can be loaded rather than compiled in.

nodes.label: SSH, in layers with test vectors
nodes.rationale: The binary packet protocol, Curve25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305, userauth, channels. The one place here where a bug is silent - a wrong nonce keeps working and is not secure - so 'it connected' is not evidence.

nodes.label: Get Info, and editing attributes from the desktop
nodes.rationale: The query engine works and nothing writes an attribute, so the search box finds only what attr put there.

nodes.label: A name in the query index
nodes.rationale: name:*.png cannot be a query today, so the search box filters locally instead. BeOS indexed name precisely so it could be one.

nodes.label: File types as a preferences application
nodes.rationale: Rather than a table compiled into the image.

nodes.label: Three to four audio underruns per 2.3 seconds
nodes.rationale: Six structural changes did not move it: the ring, the priority band, an eight-times buffer, the interrupt, the C rewrite, and measuring during play rather than after. 194 interrupts per 400 periods says the device services about two periods per raise, which is QEMU's model rather than this one.

nodes.label: One kernel check failed once
nodes.rationale: 1 of 127, and not since. The evidence was destroyed by a grep that kept only the summary line. Recorded as intermittent rather than fixed, because nothing fixed it.

nodes.label: What to do when you get stuck
nodes.rationale: Instrument over UART to the last line that executed; check barriers and cache maintenance; verify MMIO against the datasheet rather than memory; compare with QEMU if the bug is on hardware or the other way; reduce to the smallest reproduction.

nodes.label: The way out is to cut scope, not to abandon
nodes.rationale: A desktop without SMP is still a desktop, and it was one for a year.
